title: pivoting
description:
Going through this concept map I saw that it says is part of dplyr. On the Spanish version it says it part of tidyr.
I think it should say it part of tidyr in the English version too. This function works slightly different to dplyr basics (e.g. the first argument is a data frame and the subsequent arguments describe what to do with the data frame).

title: Joins
description:
I've been working on a concept map for joins. I'm similarly not completely satisfied, but I thought I would share for feedback and collaboration.

![joins](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/92617160-ffd95d80-f28c-11ea-99f6-9698de742f0c.png)

In working on this, I've realized that one conceptual challenge is that the while all joins involve two tables, the _verb_ of the operation is different for mutating and filtering joins — mutating joins _combine_ while filtering joins _filter_.

I liked and I tried to retain the table structure from [the current concept map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/concept-maps/a8694874450b353359fd2cffab3f2936fe2ff6e7/en/join.png), but I tried to incorporate the row-matching that occurs when joining tables. Although now comparing again to the current version, I've lost the filling with `NA` concept.

![current concept map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/concept-maps/a8694874450b353359fd2cffab3f2936fe2ff6e7/en/join.png)

Feedback welcome and I'll be happy to iterate on this or open a PR to submit more formally.
